light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the opening a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, small blemishes and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes with real creases, dust and wear. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the room in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural hands; people move naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

anchors.prompt: The same place as the first image — the very same room, same walls, same door, same furniture and shelves, same light — seen from a slightly different spot a little later. The presenter is the man of the reference photos — about 50, black curly hair, short greying beard, the face of the last input image — dressed in a worn olive-green work shirt with the sleeves rolled up to the elbows, stained with paint and dust, and a worn brown leather apron over it. He stands at the heavy wooden workbench in the garage workshop, a second old wooden chair lying on its side on the bench with one leg pulled out of its hole, the first chair already standing clamped at the far end of the bench, a jar of pale honey-coloured glue, a flat brush, a strip of cotton cloth, a small wooden drawer frame, a tape measure, two steel bar clamps and a damp rag; he looks at the lens. Medium shot from the waist up, the scene fills the frame.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: he holds the chair leg loosely in the hole, showing the gap with his thumb, looking at the lens. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: he holds the chair leg with a strip of cloth wrapped around its end, looking at the lens. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: he folds the damp rag, the joint clean, looking at the lens. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: he holds the tape measure stretched across the diagonal of the drawer frame, reading it. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: the heel of his hand pressing a corner of the drawer frame, looking at the lens. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: he pats the chair seat with one hand, wagging the index finger of the other, smiling at the lens. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: he holds up a small dark oak offcut, looking at the lens. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: he holds the oak offcut with its darker stained edge toward the lens, looking at it. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

Same photo, same place, same framing, a few seconds later: he wipes his hands on his leather apron, looking at the lens, thoughtful. He still wears the same worn olive-green work shirt with rolled sleeves and the brown leather apron.

clips.text: ¿Y si la pata baila porque el agujero se agrandó? La cola sola no rellena huecos grandes.
clips.action: he wiggles the chair leg in its hole to show the gap.

clips.text: Ahí envuelves la punta con una tira fina de tela de algodón encolada, o una viruta de madera, y recién ahí la metes.
clips.action: he wraps a thin strip of cotton cloth around the end of the chair leg.

clips.text: Trapo húmedo, limpio el sobrante ahora. Después, seco, se pone duro como vidrio.
clips.action: he wipes the joint with the damp rag.

clips.text: Y si lo que pegas es un cajón o un marco, antes de dejarlo en la prensa, mide las dos diagonales con la cinta.
clips.action: he stretches a tape measure diagonally across a small wooden drawer frame on the bench.

clips.text: Si las dos diagonales miden lo mismo, está a escuadra. Si no, lo empujas un poquito desde la esquina larga, antes de que seque.
clips.action: he pushes one corner of the drawer frame gently with the heel of his hand.

clips.text: Toda la noche en la prensa. Y al otro día, sin apuro: le das un día entero antes de sentarte.
clips.action: he pats the chair seat and wags his finger, smiling.

clips.text: Y si la madera es de roble o de algo parecido, oscura, prueba primero en un pedacito.
clips.action: he picks up a small offcut of dark oak from the bench.

clips.text: Porque con cal, esta cola puede manchar esas maderas de un tono más oscuro. Sobre todo si luego no la vas a pintar.
clips.action: he turns the oak offcut to show a darker stain line on its edge.

clips.text: Ahora déjame contarte lo que me pasó con una lectora, porque esto es importante.
clips.action: he puts the offcut down and wipes his hands on his apron.
